summary: This mishnah lists injuries that make an animal a treifah, which may not be eaten even after shechitah. The rule: any injury an animal could not live with makes it a treifah.

chunks.en: These make an animal a treifah:
chunks.explain: A treifah is a badly hurt animal that may not be eaten.
chunks.st: These wounds constitute tereifot in an animal, rendering them prohibited for consumption:

chunks.en: A food pipe with a hole in it,
chunks.st: A perforated gullet, where the perforation goes through the wall of the gullet,

chunks.en: or a windpipe that was cut,
chunks.st: or a cut windpipe.

chunks.en: if the skin around the brain got a hole,
chunks.st: If the membrane of the brain was perforated,

chunks.en: if the heart got a hole into its inner space,
chunks.st: or if the heart was perforated to its chamber;

chunks.en: if the backbone broke and its cord was cut,
chunks.st: if the spinal column was broken and its cord was cut;

chunks.he: נִטַּל הַכָּבֵד וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּר הֵימֶנּוּ כְלוּם,
chunks.en: if the liver was taken out and none of it was left,
chunks.st: if the liver was removed and nothing remained of it, any of these render the animal a tereifa.

chunks.en: a lung that got a hole,
chunks.st: Additionally, a lung that was perforated

chunks.en: or that is missing a piece.
chunks.st: or that was missing a piece renders the animal a tereifa.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Only if the hole goes into the air tubes.
chunks.st: It is not a tereifa unless it is perforated through to the bronchi.

chunks.en: If the stomach got a hole,
chunks.st: If the abomasum was perforated,

chunks.en: the gallbladder got a hole,
chunks.st: or the gallbladder was perforated,

chunks.en: the small intestines got a hole,
chunks.st: or the small intestines were perforated, it is a tereifa.

chunks.en: the inner stomach got a hole,
chunks.st: It is also a tereifa in a case where the internal rumen was perforated

words.note: The first, biggest stomach of a cow.

chunks.en: or most of the outer stomach was torn.
chunks.st: or where the majority of the external rumen was torn.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: In a big animal, a tear of a tefach,
chunks.st: For a large animal, a tear of one handbreadth renders it a tereifa,

words.note: About the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and in a small animal, most of it.
chunks.st: while for a small animal, it is a tereifa only if the majority of it was torn.

chunks.en: If two other parts of the stomach got a hole to the outside,
chunks.st: And it is a tereifa where the omasum [hemses] or the reticulum was perforated to the outside, i.e., to the abdominal cavity, but not if the perforation was between the two.

words.note: A part of a cow's stomach.
Beis hakosos, another part of a cow's stomach.

chunks.en: if it fell from the roof,
chunks.st: Likewise, if an animal fell from the roof,

chunks.en: if most of its ribs broke,
chunks.st: or if the majority of its ribs were fractured, or if it was

chunks.en: or a wolf clawed it.
chunks.st: clawed by a wolf, it is a tereifa.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: A wolf's clawing in a small animal,
chunks.st: If it was clawed by a wolf in the case of a small animal, i.e., a sheep or goat;

chunks.en: and a lion's clawing in a big animal,
chunks.st: or clawed by a lion in the case of a large animal, i.e., cattle;

chunks.en: a hawk's clawing in a small bird,
chunks.st: or if it was clawed by a hawk in the case of a small bird;

chunks.en: and a big bird's clawing in a big bird.
chunks.st: or if it was clawed by a large bird of prey in the case of a large bird, then it is a tereifa.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Any injury that an animal like it cannot live with makes it a treifah.
chunks.st: Any animal that was injured such that an animal in a similar condition could not live for an extended period is a tereifa, the consumption of which is forbidden by Torah law.

summary: This mishnah lists injuries that do not make an animal a treifah, like a small hole in the windpipe, a missing spleen or kidneys, or a cracked skull without a hole in the skin of the brain.

chunks.en: And these are kosher in an animal:
chunks.st: And these, despite their condition, are kosher in an animal:

chunks.en: The windpipe got a hole or a crack.
chunks.st: If its windpipe was perforated or cracked lengthwise.

chunks.en: How much can be missing?
chunks.st: How much can the windpipe be missing and still be kosher?

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Up to the size of an Italian issar coin.
chunks.st: Until the perforation is the same size as the Italian issar.

chunks.en: The skull broke but there was no hole
chunks.st: If the skull was fractured but

chunks.en: in the skin of the brain,
chunks.st: the membrane of the brain was not perforated, it is kosher.

chunks.en: the heart got a hole, but not into its inner space,
chunks.st: If the heart was perforated and the perforation did not reach its chamber,

chunks.he: נִשְׁבְּרָה הַשִּׁדְרָה וְלֹא נִפְסַק הַחוּט שֶׁלָּהּ,
chunks.en: the backbone broke but its cord was not cut,
chunks.st: or if the spinal column was broken but its cord was not cut,

chunks.en: the liver was taken out and a kezayis of it was left,
chunks.st: or if the liver was removed and an olive-bulk of it remained, it is kosher.

words.note: A kezayis, the size of an olive.

chunks.en: two parts of the stomach that got a hole
chunks.st: Additionally, it is kosher if the omasum or the reticulum was perforated

chunks.en: one into the other,
chunks.st: one into the other.

chunks.en: the spleen was taken out,
chunks.st: If the spleen was removed,

chunks.en: the kidneys were taken out,
chunks.st: or the kidneys were removed,

chunks.en: the lower jaw was taken off,
chunks.st: or if its lower jaw was removed,

chunks.en: its womb was taken out,
chunks.st: or if its womb was removed,

chunks.en: or its lung shriveled by the hand of Heaven.
chunks.st: or if its lung shriveled by the hand of Heaven, the animal is kosher.

chunks.en: An animal whose skin came off: Rabbi Meir says it is kosher,
chunks.st: In the case of an animal whose hide was removed, Rabbi Meir deems it kosher,

chunks.en: and the Sages say it is pasul.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it a tereifa and unfit for consumption.

summary: This mishnah lists injuries that make a bird a treifah. A bird that was crushed and is still twitching is a treifah, unless it lived for a full day afterward.

chunks.en: And these make a bird a treifah:
chunks.st: And these are tereifot in a bird:

chunks.en: A food pipe with a hole,
chunks.st: One with a perforated gullet,

chunks.en: a cut windpipe,
chunks.st: or with a cut windpipe that was cut across its width;

chunks.en: a weasel hit it on its head
chunks.st: or if a weasel struck the bird on its head

chunks.en: in a place that makes it a treifah,
chunks.st: in a place that renders it a tereifa, as one must be concerned that the membrane of the brain was perforated;

chunks.en: the gizzard got a hole,
chunks.st: or if the gizzard was perforated;

chunks.en: the small intestines got a hole.
chunks.st: or if the small intestines were perforated.

chunks.en: If it fell into the fire and its insides were scorched,
chunks.st: In a case where a bird fell into the fire and its innards were singed [neḥmeru],

chunks.en: if they are green,
chunks.st: if they turned green

chunks.en: they are pasul. If they are red,
chunks.st: they are unfit, and the bird is a tereifa, but if they are red the bird is

chunks.en: they are kosher.
chunks.st: kosher.

chunks.en: If someone stepped on it,
chunks.st: If a person trampled the bird,

chunks.en: or banged it against a wall,
chunks.st: or slammed it against a wall,

chunks.en: or an animal crushed it and it is twitching,
chunks.st: or if an animal crushed it and it is twitching, it is a tereifa because its limbs were shattered.

chunks.en: but it lasted a full day and then he shechted it, it is kosher.
chunks.st: But if the bird lasted for a twenty-four-hour period, and then one slaughtered it, it is kosher.

words.note: A full day of twenty-four hours.

summary: This mishnah lists injuries that do not make a bird a treifah, like a hole in its crop, broken wings or legs, or plucked wing feathers.

chunks.en: And these are kosher in a bird:
chunks.st: And these are kosher among birds:

chunks.en: The windpipe got a hole or a crack,
chunks.st: If a bird’s windpipe was perforated or cracked lengthwise;

chunks.en: a weasel hit it on its head
chunks.st: or if a weasel struck the bird on its head

chunks.en: in a place that does not make it a treifah,
chunks.st: in a place that does not render it a tereifa;

chunks.en: the crop got a hole.
chunks.explain: The crop is a pouch in a bird's neck where food waits.
chunks.st: or if the crop was perforated.

chunks.en: Rebbi says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: It is kosher

chunks.en: Even if it was taken out.
chunks.st: even if the crop was removed.

chunks.en: Its insides came out but did not get a hole,
chunks.st: If the bird’s intestines emerged from the abdominal wall but were not perforated,

chunks.en: its wings broke,
chunks.st: or if its wings were broken,

chunks.en: its legs broke,
chunks.st: or if its legs were broken,

chunks.en: its wing feathers were plucked.
chunks.st: or if the feathers on its wings were plucked, the bird is kosher.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If its soft feathers were taken off, it is pasul.
chunks.st: If the down covering its body was removed, it is a tereifa and unfit for consumption.

words.note: The soft feathers on a bird's body.

summary: An animal that is sick from things like smoke, cold, or bad food or water is still kosher. But one that ate poison or was bitten by a snake may not be eaten, because it is dangerous.

chunks.en: An animal with too much blood,
chunks.st: With regard to an animal that is congested with excess blood,

chunks.en: or that breathed in smoke, or that got chilled,
chunks.st: or that was smoked, i.e., that suffered from smoke inhalation, or that was chilled and subsequently became sick,

chunks.en: or that ate a poison plant,
chunks.st: or that ate oleander, which is poisonous,

chunks.en: or that ate chicken droppings,
chunks.st: or that ate the excrement of chickens,

chunks.en: or that drank bad water,
chunks.st: or that drank foul water,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה. אָכְלָה סַם הַמָּוֶת אוֹ שֶׁהִכִּישָׁהּ נָחָשׁ,
chunks.en: it is kosher. If it ate deadly poison or a snake bit it,
chunks.st: although in all these cases the animal is in danger, it is kosher. By contrast, if the animal ate deadly poison, or if a snake bit the animal,

chunks.en: it is allowed as far as treifah goes,
chunks.st: with regard to the prohibition of tereifa, consumption of the animal would be permitted,

chunks.en: but it is forbidden because it is dangerous to life.
chunks.st: but it is prohibited due to the threat to one’s life if he eats it.

summary: The Torah gives the signs of kosher animals, but not of kosher birds. The Sages taught signs: a bird that claws its food is not kosher; one with an extra toe, a crop, and a peelable gizzard is kosher.

chunks.he: סִימָנֵי בְהֵמָה וְחַיָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
chunks.en: The signs of kosher animals and wild animals were said in the Torah,
chunks.st: The signs that indicate that a domesticated animal and an undomesticated animal are kosher were stated in the Torah,

chunks.en: but the signs of a bird were not said.
chunks.st: and the signs of a kosher bird were not explicitly stated.

chunks.en: But the Sages said:
chunks.st: But the Sages stated certain signs in a bird:

chunks.en: Any bird that claws its food
chunks.st: Any bird that claws its prey and eats it

chunks.he: טָמֵא. כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ אֶצְבַּע יְתֵרָה,
chunks.en: is not kosher. Any bird that has an extra toe,
chunks.st: is non-kosher. Any bird that has an extra digit behind the leg slightly elevated above the other digits,

chunks.en: and a crop, and its gizzard peels,
chunks.st: and a crop, which is a sack alongside the gullet in which food is stored prior to digestion, and for which the yellowish membrane inside its gizzard can be peeled,

chunks.he: טָהוֹר. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: is kosher. Rabbi Eliezer the son of Tzadok says:
chunks.st: is kosher. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:

chunks.he: כָּל עוֹף הַחוֹלֵק אֶת רַגְלָיו, טָמֵא:
chunks.en: Any bird that splits its feet is not kosher.
chunks.explain: When it stands on a string, it puts two toes on each side.
chunks.st: Any bird that splits the digits of its feet when standing on a string, placing two digits on one side of the string and two on the other, is non-kosher.

summary: The Sages gave signs for kosher grasshoppers: four legs, four wings, two jumping legs, and wings that cover most of the body. A kosher fish has fins and scales.

chunks.he: וּבַחֲגָבִים, כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ אַרְבַּע רַגְלַיִם,
chunks.en: And with grasshoppers: any that has four legs,
chunks.st: And with regard to grasshoppers, whose signs were also not stated in the Torah, the Sages stated: Any grasshopper that has four legs,

chunks.en: and four wings,
chunks.st: and four wings,

chunks.en: and jumping legs, and its wings cover most of it.
chunks.st: and two additional jumping legs, and whose wings cover most of its body, is kosher.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: And its name must be "chagav".
chunks.explain: Chagav is the Hebrew word for a kind of grasshopper.
chunks.st: And this applies only if the name of its species is grasshopper.

chunks.he: וּבַדָּגִים, כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ סְנַפִּיר וְקַשְׂקָשֶׂת.
chunks.en: And with fish: any that has a fin and a scale.
chunks.st: And with regard to fish, the signs are explicitly stated in the Torah: Any fish that has a fin and a scale is kosher;

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Two scales and one fin.
chunks.st: Two scales and one fin.

chunks.en: And these are scales:
chunks.st: And these are scales:

chunks.en: the ones that are stuck on its body.
chunks.st: Those that are fixed to its body;

chunks.en: And fins are what it swims with.
chunks.st: and fins are those with which the fish swims.
